title: Found a cheap Bloomberg-style real-time news trading dashboard/API
author: bjxxjj
selftext:
https://preview.redd.it/c7h94d9hcevh1.png?width=1080&format=png&auto=webp&s=60d3fead58a8f119cd5882f43c11fbeef42d567e

I was looking for a more affordable way to monitor real-time market news for algo trading, and I came across this:

[https://tradingnews.press/](https://tradingnews.press/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

At first I thought it was just another financial news API, but the dashboard caught my attention.

It looks more like a lightweight event-driven trading terminal:

* live WebSocket news feed
* breaking news detection
* ticker extraction
* sentiment / direction analysis
* latency tracking from source → API
* paper trading simulation
* strategy signals generated from news events

The interesting part is the pipeline:

**News → Event Detection → Sentiment → Trading Signal → Paper Execution**

The screenshot shows things like:

* live wires from TradingNews feed
* LONG/SHORT signals
* simulated fills and P&L
* equity curve
* Sharpe ratio / drawdown tracking

Basically it seems designed for people building:

* algorithmic trading strategies
* AI trading agents
* news-based strategies
* market monitoring bots

The pricing is also much lower than most institutional-grade financial data products:

$14/month starter  
$35/month for real-time WebSocket access

Obviously this isn't replacing Bloomberg or Reuters, but for developers who just want structured market news without paying enterprise prices, it looks interesting.

Curious if anyone here is already using news-based signals in their algo strategies?

What data points would you want from a real-time financial news API?

comments.author: leroylabs
comments.body: The fields I would want most are source publication time, API receipt time, update/correction IDs, original text, extracted ticker with confidence, and a stable event ID for deduplication. The source-to-API latency number is much less useful if revisions or syndicated copies become separate “breaking” events. For the News → Sentiment → Paper Execution pipeline, I’d also want an event-time replay endpoint plus the contemporaneous bid/ask, so a LONG/SHORT signal can be tested at the price actually available after delivery. The screenshot is unavailable here, so I cannot tell whether its fills or Sharpe calculation already account for that delay.
